requirement: Open a list of context-manager resources as one bundle: if any fails, close the ones already opened in reverse order and raise a wrapped error; on success keep them open until the bundle is closed.
skeleton: ResourceBundle.acquire entering factories on an ExitStack, wrapping failures in AcquireError, transferring the stack with pop_all, and closing on exit.
caption: A standard-library helper that acquires several context-managed resources as one all-or-nothing bundle. The module defines a Factory alias for a zero-argument callable returning an AbstractContextManager, an AcquireError subclass of RuntimeError, and a ResourceBundle class holding an ExitStack and the list of entered resources. The classmethod acquire(factories) raises ValueError saying at least one factory is required when the sequence is empty. Otherwise it opens an ExitStack in a with block and enters each factory's context manager with enter_context, collecting the values. When a factory fails, the exception is wrapped in AcquireError naming the zero-based resource index, chained from the original, and leaving the with block unwinds the stack so every resource already opened is closed in reverse order. When all succeed it calls pop_all to move the callbacks to a fresh stack, so leaving the block closes nothing, and returns a bundle that owns that stack. close() closes the held stack, and the bundle is itself a context manager whose __exit__ always calls close. The fixture uses recording context managers and asserts that two resources open in order and close in reverse when the with block ends, that a third failing factory raises AcquireError mentioning resource 2 failed with an OSError cause after closing cache and then db, that an acquired bundle stays open until close is called, and that an empty list raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Acquire a list of resources together or not at all
constraints: An empty factory list raises ValueError
A failing factory raises AcquireError naming its index, chained from the cause
Resources opened before the failure are closed in reverse order
A successful bundle keeps its resources open until close or the end of its with block

rationale.teaches: ExitStack as an all-or-nothing acquisition scope, with pop_all transferring ownership once every resource is open.
rationale.why: Nested with blocks cannot express a variable number of resources, and a hand-written loop leaks whatever it opened before the failure. Only a fixture that records open and close events can tell a leak from a premature close.

ops.docstring: Acquire several context managers together and release them in reverse on failure.

ops.source:
class AcquireError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when one resource in a bundle cannot be acquired."""

candidates.why_wrong: An empty factory list returns an empty bundle instead of raising, so a misconfigured caller runs with no resources.
The bundle keeps the original stack instead of the popped one, so every resource is closed the moment acquire returns.
close detaches the callbacks without running them, so no resource is ever closed.
The error counts resources from one, so it names the wrong resource as the one that failed.
Leaving the bundle's with block closes resources only when an exception is propagating, so a normal exit leaks them.
